extracted.intended_audience: readers of Spanish-language political opinion (academics, activists, journalists, informed public interested in Catalan politics and nationalism)
extracted.subtask_description: Opinion/analytical pieces evaluating arguments and rhetoric used by Catalan nationalist actors (manifestos, politicians, academics), focusing on xenophobia, language policy, historical claims, and political consequences. Targets critique of public discourse rather than academic peer-review per se.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid racist/biological determinism
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not make or normalize claims like “probablemente la inteligencia es [determinada genéticamente]” or “El cociente intelectual de los negros de Estados Unidos es inferior al de los blancos”.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page condemns statements that essentialize groups by race or genetics as unacceptable and pseudo‑scientific; such claims are given as examples of xenophobic/ racist rhetoric and should be rejected outright.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject alignment with xenophobic figures
rubrics_metrics.description: “Resulta absolutamente inaceptable que los partidos y formaciones de izquierda en Cataluña se alineen con semejantes personajes y sus secuaces” (referring to xenophobic leaders).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Political parties and left formations should not ally themselves with or legitimize xenophobic actors; doing so undermines principles and is ethically unacceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use rigorous empirical comparison for socioeconomic claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Critique of: “Afirmar... que un pensionista catalán... recibe en realidad menos dinero... raya la demagogia y la falta de rigor.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When comparing regions (e.g., pensions, cost of living), use robust metrics: compare pension distributions, means/medians, percentages by pension brackets, poverty and exclusion rates, and provide appropriate context instead of simplistic claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid denigrating regional/ class-based stereotypes
rubrics_metrics.description: Against rhetoric like calling Extremadurans/Andalusians lazy or “amantes del no trabajar” (PEES/PEASANT) or describing whole groups as “hombre destruido... anárquico.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rely on derogatory stereotyping of whole regions or classes; such rhetoric is insulting, politically divisive, and undermines solidarity among working classes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge and substantiate media-visibility and representation claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Observation: “El diferente trato mediático... que reciben las regiones españolas es especialmente sangrante... ¿Cuántas veces sale en las noticias nacionales Extremadura?”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If arguing media bias or differential visibility, support claims with data on coverage frequency, mention specific omissions, and avoid emotive generalizations without evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid essentialist claims about integration/difficulty of assimilation
rubrics_metrics.description: Critique of statements like “es más difícil integrar a un latinoamericano que a un andaluz” and arguments framing certain populations as inherently harder to integrate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Integration should not be portrayed as dependent on immutable ethnic or regional traits; such essentialism fuels exclusion and justifies discriminatory policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not weaponize history into a static, exclusionary national identity
rubrics_metrics.description: Against using historical narratives (e.g., 1714) to construct a petrified, immutable Catalan identity that excludes others: “El concepto... petrificado, inmóvil...”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historical arguments must be nuanced; avoid circular reasoning that uses selective history to legitimize present exclusionary policies or territorial claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish academic language from political intent; disclose affiliations
rubrics_metrics.description: “Se trata de una declaración política... firmado por algunos filólogos con conocida activa militancia política... y responsabilidades gubernamentales pasadas...”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When academics intervene in public debates, be transparent about political commitments and institutional dependencies (e.g., funding, positions) so the claim is not presented as neutral purely on academic authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make implicit consequences explicit and examine policy implications
rubrics_metrics.description: Warning that arguments have “consecuencias lógicas... implícitas” such as assimilation becoming exclusion: “Por ese camino la integración se convierte en asimilación y abre la puerta a la marginación o exclusión de los no asimilados.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate proposals by spelling out likely consequences (intended and unintended), especially risks of marginalization, loss of rights, or social exclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid framing bilingualism as coercive blame against immigrants
rubrics_metrics.description: Critique of phrasing like “el mecanisme... la bilingüización forzosa de la población” and “instrument involuntari de colonització lingüística” attributed to immigrants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Language policy debates should avoid assigning blame to immigrant populations for shifts in language use; distinguish coercive state policies from migration-driven language change and recognize immigrants' contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure historical claims are supported by primary sources and nuance
rubrics_metrics.description: Rebuttal of the manifesto’s claim that bilingualism was precarious until 1939: “Falso. ... El bilingüismo estaba bien presente... entre las clases populares urbanas de Cataluña mucho antes de 1939.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historical assertions (e.g., prevalence of languages) must cite documentary evidence (newspapers, union records, archival sources) and avoid sweeping statements contradicted by historical record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid euphemistic or ambiguous wording that conceals exclusionary aims
rubrics_metrics.description: The manifesto eludes using explicit terms (e.g., official language) and employs euphemisms: “la proposición final... elude utilizar expresamente el término de lengua oficial... adopta el concepto bajo la identificación de una sola lengua como natural del país.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be clear about policy proposals; do not mask exclusive aims through equivocal language—expose what a proposal would mean in practice (e.g., effects on rights, services).

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not present academic consensus where dependency biases exist
rubrics_metrics.description: Observation that the 280 signatories “en su inmensa mayoría dependientes de la Generalitat, como funcionarios, asesores o subvencionados” which can bias representation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check for conflicts of interest and institutional dependency when assessing the representativeness or neutrality of an academic statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Favor policies implemented by consensus and democratic means over coercion
rubrics_metrics.description: On language immersion and control: “¿Y eso se resuelve imponiendo un monolingüismo básico? ¿Mediante decisiones de autoridad o por políticas de consenso?” and warning that obsessively controlling private language use is “una puerta abierta al totalitarismo comunitario.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design language and cultural policies through participatory, consensual democratic processes rather than top‑down mandates that intrude on private life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criticize demagogy and demand intellectual rigor from public intellectuals
rubrics_metrics.description: Accusation that some arguments are “demagógicas” or of “penuria intelectual” and that public intellectuals should not resort to slogans or crude narratives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public commentary should avoid demagogy and instead display historical awareness, methodological care, and proportionality; invoke evidence and reasoned argument rather than blanket denunciations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not shut down public debate by labelling political interventions as merely academic
rubrics_metrics.description: “La interpretación del President Puigdemont... puede entenderse como una manera de zanjar un incipiente debate, pero también de cerrarlo aceptando la invocada razón académica.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Political actors and institutions should not use 'academic' framing to silence criticism; distinguish genuine scholarly debate from political positioning and allow open contestation.
